q: While examining the jugular venous pulse, the c wave is produced by bulging of which structure into the atrium during the isovolumetric phase of ventricular contraction?
o: Tricuspid valve into the right atrium
Mitral valve into the left atrium
Aortic valve into the left ventricle
Pulmonary valve into the right ventricle
ex: The c wave of the JVP marks displacement of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium during isovolumetric ventricular contraction.

q: In sinoatrial nodal pacemaker cells, the slow diastolic (phase 4) depolarization that sets intrinsic heart rate is initiated chiefly by which current?
ex: The funny current If plus decaying K+ conductance generate SA node diastolic depolarization; IK1 is absent in pacemaker cells.

q: Blood flow through the left coronary artery is maximal during which phase of the cardiac cycle?
ex: Systolic compression of subendocardial vessels limits flow, so left coronary flow peaks during diastole.

q: When arterial pressure suddenly falls, the baroreceptor reflex acts to return pressure toward baseline. Which type of physiological control is this?
ex: The baroreflex opposes any pressure disturbance, the defining feature of negative feedback control.

q: By Fick principle, oxygen consumption is 250 mL/min while the arterial and mixed venous oxygen contents are 20 and 15 mL/dL respectively. The cardiac output is closest to:
ex: CO = VO2/(CaO2-CvO2); with an a-v oxygen gap of 5 vol%, cardiac output is about 5 L/min.

q: For a healthy young adult with a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, the approximate mean arterial pressure is:
ex: MAP = DBP + (SBP-DBP)/3; here 90 + 20 = 110 mmHg.

q: The vascular segment providing the greatest fraction of systemic vascular resistance, hence a main target of blood-pressure control, is:
ex: Arterioles contribute the majority of total systemic resistance.

q: Functional residual capacity equals the arithmetic sum of which two volumes?
o: Inspiratory reserve volume + expiratory reserve volume
ex: FRC = ERV + RV; it is the lung volume present at the end of a quiet expiration.

q: Deoxygenated blood carries appreciably more CO2 than oxygenated blood at the same partial pressure. This property of hemoglobin is the:
ex: Reduced hemoglobin binds CO2 and H+ better than oxyhemoglobin, which aids CO2 uptake in the veins.

q: Which receptors are chiefly stimulated by a fall in arterial PO2 (hypoxemia) and drive the hyperventilation of high altitude?
ex: Peripheral chemoreceptors, especially the carotid body, are the principal sensors of arterial hypoxemia.

q: The stimulus sensed by the central chemoreceptors that closely tracks arterial PCO2 changes is:
o: Hydrogen ion concentration of the cerebrospinal fluid
ex: CO2 crosses the blood-brain barrier and hydrates to liberate H+; CSF H+ is the real stimulus of central chemoreceptors.

q: A trekker develops headache, breathlessness and cerebral edema after rapid ascent above 3000 m. Which of the following is NOT part of standard management?
ex: Acute mountain sickness is managed with descent, O2, acetazolamide and dexamethasone; digoxin has no role.

q: Compared with a healthy lung, the static compliance of the lungs in emphysema is characteristically:
o: Raised only when gas trapping occurs
ex: Emphysema destroys elastic tissue, raising compliance; fibrosis instead lowers it.

q: At the end of a quiet expiration, the intrapleural pressure in a healthy adult is closest to:
ex: Resting intrapleural pressure is roughly -5 mmHg, keeping the lung partly distended at FRC.

q: The counter-current multiplier that concentrates urine operates principally in which nephron segment?
o: Loop of Henle, mainly its thick ascending limb
ex: NaCl transport out of the thick ascending limb builds the medullary osmotic gradient.

q: Creatinine clearance slightly OVERESTIMATES the true GFR because:
o: Creatinine is actively secreted by renal tubules
Creatinine is reabsorbed along the nephron
Creatinine is stored in the renal medulla
ex: Mild tubular secretion of creatinine makes its clearance exceed the actual GFR.

q: Renal plasma flow is best approximated by the clearance of which substance?
ex: PAH is almost completely removed in a single pass through the kidney, so PAH clearance equals renal plasma flow.

q: Body fluid analysis shows: sodium 12 mEq/L, potassium 140 mEq/L, chloride 4 mmol/L. This represents:
ex: High potassium with low sodium marks the intracellular composition.

q: The normal insensible water loss from the skin and respiratory tract each day is closest to:
ex: Insensible loss is on the order of 500-700 mL/day and cannot be regulated.

q: A middle-aged woman leaks small volumes of urine only on coughing or straining. The most likely diagnosis is:
ex: Sudden intra-abdominal pressure overcomes a weakened sphincter, producing stress incontinence.

q: ADH promotes water reabsorption in the collecting duct by inserting which channel at the apical membrane?
ex: Vasopressin moves AQP-2 water channels into the luminal membrane of collecting-duct principal cells.

q: During intestinal peristalsis, the segment aboral (downstream) to the food bolus relaxes mainly because of which mediator?
ex: VIP relaxes the segment ahead of the bolus during peristalsis.

q: After a fatty meal, gall bladder contraction is chiefly triggered by which hormone?
ex: CCK contracts the gall bladder and promotes pancreatic enzyme secretion.

q: Which sequence best describes the order of motor events during vomiting?
o: Reverse peristalsis of small intestine, LES closure, gastric contraction, UES relaxation, then inspiration against closed glottis
Pyloric relaxation, reverse peristalsis, inspiration with closed glottis, gastric contraction
Gastric contraction, LES relaxation, reverse peristalsis, UES relaxation
Inspiration with closed glottis occurs first, then gastric emptying
ex: Vomiting classically runs: small-intestine reverse peristalsis, LES closure, gastric contraction, UES relaxation, then forced inspiration against the closed glottis at ejection.

q: The receptor that mediates the metabolic actions of insulin on target cells is best described as:
ex: The insulin receptor is an alpha2-beta2 receptor tyrosine kinase.

q: Which hormone acts on a receptor located INSIDE the cell?
ex: Lipophilic thyroxine diffuses into the cell and binds its nuclear receptor.

q: For equal glucose loads, the plasma insulin rise is greater when glucose is taken by mouth than given intravenously. The reason is:
o: The incretin effect of GIP and GLP-1
The liver trapping more glucose after an oral load
Lower renal loss of the oral glucose
Suppression of glucagon by gastric acidity
ex: Gut incretins (GIP, GLP-1) potentiate insulin secretion after oral glucose.

q: Plasma prolactin levels are highest at approximately which time?
ex: The postpartum prolactin surge (about 24 h) initiates lactation; sleep also raises prolactin.

q: Secretion of aldosterone occurs from which zone of the adrenal gland?
ex: Aldosterone is the product of the outermost zona glomerulosa.

q: Somatostatin within the pancreatic islets is produced by which cell type?
ex: Islet delta cells release somatostatin, which inhibits both insulin and glucagon.

q: The circadian peak of plasma cortisol in a normal day-night cycle occurs at approximately:
ex: Cortisol secretion peaks in the early-morning hours and declines through the day.

q: The resting membrane potential of an excitable cell is largely set by the resting conductance of which ion?
ex: At rest the membrane behaves almost as a potassium electrode, so the RMP sits near the K+ equilibrium potential.

q: During the ABSOLUTE refractory period a neuron cannot discharge a new action potential mainly because:
o: Voltage-gated Na+ channels are in the inactivated state
The Na-K ATPase pump stops working
ex: Na+ channel inactivation renders the membrane absolutely inexcitable.

q: A patient has hyperkalemia with serum potassium 7 mEq/L. The expected effect on resting potential and action-potential generation is:
o: Depolarizes the resting potential and makes spikes harder to generate
Hyperpolarizes the resting potential and makes spikes easier to generate
ex: High extracellular K+ partially depolarizes the membrane toward threshold and inactivates some Na+ channels, blunting excitability.

q: In the actin-myosin cross-bridge cycle, detachment of myosin heads from actin requires:
o: The binding of a fresh ATP molecule to the myosin head
Rise and fall of sarcoplasmic calcium
Dissociation of ADP and phosphate from the head
ex: The rigor state persists until a new ATP binds the myosin head and detaches the cross-bridge.

q: Which nerve fiber conducts impulses at the highest velocity (about 120 m/s) and transmits muscle-spindle afferents?
ex: Group Ia fibers are the largest myelinated afferents, conducting near 120 m/s.

q: After a night of sleeping with an arm under the head, a person wakes with arm weakness but no numbness. The best explanation is:
o: Large myelinated A fibers are more susceptible to pressure than unmyelinated C fibers
C fibers are more easily compressed than any other fiber
B fibers fail even before A fibers under pressure
C and A fibers show identical pressure sensitivity
ex: Compression blocks the large myelinated motor fibers first while pain-carrying C fibers survive, giving paresis without numbness.

q: In excitation-contraction coupling of skeletal muscle, calcium released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum switches the contraction on by binding directly to:
ex: Ca2+ binds troponin C, moving tropomyosin to expose the myosin-binding sites of actin.

q: A patient develops involuntary violent flinging movements confined to one side after a stroke. The likely lesion is in the:
ex: Contralateral hemiballismus localizes to the subthalamic nucleus.

q: The spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve mediates which sensory modality?
o: Pain and temperature from the face
ex: Pain and temperature fibers of the trigeminal nerve descend to end in its spinal nucleus.

q: The hippocampus plays its most classically pivotal role in:
o: Encoding and consolidating new long-term memories
ex: The hippocampus is central to the consolidation of new episodic memories.

q: Parkinson disease is classically caused by loss of dopamine neurons in which brain region?
ex: Loss of the nigro-striatal dopamine pathway is the hallmark of Parkinson disease.

q: The sympathetic innervation of eccrine sweat glands is unusual because the transmitter acting on the gland is:
ex: Eccrine sweat glands receive sympathetic cholinergic fibers acting on muscarinic receptors, the classic exception.

q: Hemisection of the right half of the cervical cord (Brown-Sequard syndrome) typically produces:
o: Ipsilateral loss of touch-vibration-proprioception plus contralateral loss of pain-temperature below the lesion
Contralateral paralysis with ipsilateral pain loss
Bilateral flaccid paralysis below the lesion
Loss of light touch, pain and temperature all on the contralateral side
ex: Hemisection spares the ipsilateral dorsal columns/pyramidal tract and the opposite spinothalamic tract, hence dissociated crossed sensory loss.

q: In the dark-adapted eye, night vision and sensitivity to very low light intensities are provided mainly by:
ex: Rods and their visual pigment rhodopsin subserve scotopic dim-light vision.
